Principle 10: My School Days and My Days in Military Service
My Early Childhood School Days
When I was young, I was not good at studying.
I was not good at taking tests and was often scolded by my parents and teachers.
I just wanted to play with my friends.
My Youth in Middle School
For me, puberty came early, but I did not have many problems with this.
My life at this time of life was similar to others.
I was really interested in listening to music and watching movies.
I was trying to work hard in school, so I could get into a good high school, but I had a very hard time doing so.
My Difficult Time in High School
In high school, I spent my time wandering around with my friends.
At this point in my life, my parents and upper classmates gave me good advice about how to change my life for the better.
This really helped me to get back on track with my studies.
Then, I started to really prepare to enter a good university.
When we are young we do not realize how important this time is to our future.
I am really glad I had people to help me find my way.
My Life as a University Student
During my freshman and sophomore years in college, I made lots of friends and joined many clubs.
Once again, I was not interested in studying very hard.
When I was in high school, my dream was to be an English teacher, but I learned I was not very good at English, and I did not want to study hard enough to fulfill this dream.
I changed my major to Engineering and really liked it.
Serving Time in the Military
After my sophomore year, I took a leave of absence from my studies and got a part-time job for six months before I started my military service.
My military service was a hard time in my life, but I learned a lot.
During this time, I developed patience and an understanding of how important my family was.
After my military service was completed, I returned to my studies once again.
